contents.content: Write a letter to your future self!
Instructions: Complete the following steps. Fill in the Self Assessment.

images.text:
Kristi's Mom: So, Kristi, what do you plan on doing next?
Kristi: Beats me. I'm young, I'm just going to take it day by day.
Kristi's Mom: Kristi, you can't just sit around and wait for a job. You have got to look. What do you intend to do?
Kristi: Good question. I'm thinking of looking online.
Kristi's Mom: That's a good idea. What kind of job are you thinking of applying for?

Kristi: How should I know? I'd like to do something that's related to journalism or public relations maybe.
Kristi's Mom: How about becoming a news reporter? It would be so lovely to see you on TV every day.
Kristi: Definitely not! I'd like to do something that's more behind the scenes.
Kristi's Mom: What were you thinking then?
Kristi: It's hard to say ... I guess it depends on the kind of jobs that are out there.
Kristi's Mom: Well, you remember my friend Danielle? She works at a radio station. She's the programming coordinator for the station. I could talk to her if you'd like.

Kristi: That's alright, Mom. I'm actually hoping to work for a publication.
Kristi's Mom: What kind of publication were you thinking?
Kristi: Your guess is as good as mine. I just hope to find a job sooner rather than later.
Kristi's Mom: A newspaper, maybe a magazine?
Kristi: Right now it's anyone's guess, really.
Kristi's Mom: What are you going to do about that? You need to be more proactive.
Kristi: I know, Mom. I'm going to do some research online this afternoon. I'm planning to create a shortlist of the jobs that I feel suit me better. Then, I intend to apply for each one of them.
Kristi's Mom: That's a good plan. I would like to help. I'm thinking of giving you a hand with your research. What's the best website for jobs?
Kristi: Don't ask me.

There are other verbs and patterns you can use to express hope and expectations for the future apart from using the Future tense .

You can use:
  • hope + to + verb
  • (be) + plan (-ing) + to + verb / (be) + plan (-ing) + on + verb-ing
  • be going to + verb
  • would like + to + verb
  • intend + to + verb thinking of + verb-ing

When talking to people, you may find you are asked difficult questions.  If you are not sure about the answer, there are different ways to respond to say you “don't know” the answer.
Here are some ways to respond to difficult questions:

• Beats me!
  • Good question.
  • Who knows?
  • How should I know?
  • Maybe?
  • It's hard to say …
  • I guess it depends.
  • Your guess is as good as mine.
  • I have no idea.
  • It's anyone's guess, really.
  • Don't ask me.
